newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up as foreign investors emerge.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up as foreign investors emerge.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 1.41 percent on Friday as foreign investors kept pouring money into shares of newly privatised companies, traders said.

"Finally, foreign investors are showing some interest in our shares, and it is increasing from day to day. Next week shares may fall slightly in a technical reaction, but generally I expect the rising trend to continue," said Karmen Korbun, a trader at Creditanstalt.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 12.83 points to 925.72.
* 13 shares rose and six fell, while five were untraded.
* Turnover fell to 153.9 million tolars from 162.9 million.
* Newly listed shares of drug maker Lek were the most actively traded, firming 7.79 percent to 15,003 tolars on volume of 5,862 shares for total turnover of 87.9 million tolars.
* Prefered shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the biggest gainer, firming 9.93 percent to 10,290 tolars on volume of 230 shares for total turnover of 2.4 million tolars.

* Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, falling 9.75 percent to 15,848 tolars on volume of 50 shares for total turnover of 792,000 tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
